stories.title: Fuel Truck Fire in Cairo Kills 31 and Injures 21
stories.summary: A fuel tanker overturned on a major highway near Cairo, igniting a massive fire that engulfed over two dozen vehicles. At least 31 people have died and 21 others were injured in the incident. Authorities have detained a driver suspected of causing the crash, who reportedly confessed to speeding and clipping the tanker while overtaking traffic.

stories.title: Gérard Depardieu Ordered to Stand Trial for Rape and Sexual Assault
stories.summary: Gérard Depardieu, the renowned French actor, has been ordered to stand trial for allegedly raping actress Charlotte Arnould at his Paris home in 2018. The Paris Court of Appeal upheld the decision, which comes shortly after Depardieu abandoned an appeal in a separate sexual assault conviction. If found guilty, he could face a significant prison sentence.

stories.title: Two Italians Killed in Iranian Drone Attack in Kuwait, Iran Denies Involvement
stories.summary: An Iranian drone attack on a military facility in Kuwait resulted in the deaths of two Italian workers and injuries to four others. The victims were technicians employed by a German company. Iran has denied any involvement in the incident, which has drawn international attention.

stories.title: Federal Judge Halts FCC's Early Review of ABC Broadcast Licenses
stories.summary: A federal judge has issued a temporary restraining order preventing the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses. The judge's decision supports ABC's claim that the Trump administration's actions were intended to suppress the network's free speech rights. The ruling highlights concerns over the administration's public criticisms of the network.

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau Military Leaders Postpone Elections to 2028
stories.summary: Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have announced a two-year delay for presidential and parliamentary elections, now scheduled for November 2028. This decision comes one year after the military took control of the country, with leaders citing insufficient conditions for holding elections at this time.

stories.title: Andy Taylor, Duran Duran Guitarist, Passes Away at 65
stories.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the iconic 1980s new wave band Duran Duran, has died at the age of 65 after a battle with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer. His family and the band confirmed his passing, highlighting his contributions to the band's success with hits like 'Hungry Like the Wolf' and 'Rio.'

stories.title: Trump Calls for Putin to Reduce Military Aggression in Europe
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that he urged Russian President Vladimir Putin to reduce military aggression in Europe. He expressed optimism about the potential for a quick deal between Russia and Ukraine to prevent further escalation of the conflict. Trump shared his comments on his Truth Social account but did not clarify what he meant by 'territories throughout Europe.'

stories.title: Kim Jong Un Promises to Expand North Korea's Nuclear Arsenal Amid U.S. Tensions
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has vowed to increase the country's nuclear weapons production in response to perceived threats from the United States and South Korea. This announcement follows his recent disregard for an overture from U.S. President Donald Trump to meet during Trump's visit to Asia. Kim visited facilities involved in producing nuclear materials, emphasizing the need to bolster North Korea's military capabilities.

stories.title: FCC Approves SpaceX's Plan for 1 Million Satellites, Sparking Scientific Skepticism
stories.summary: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites intended to function as data centers in space. stories.title: Diesel Tanker Capsizes Off Ibiza, One Crew Member Dies
stories.summary: A Maltese-flagged diesel tanker carrying approximately 7,000 tonnes of fuel capsized off the coast of Ibiza. While all 17 crew members were rescued, one later died in the hospital. Spanish authorities are now implementing a contingency plan to address potential marine pollution risks.

stories.title: Pittsburgh Steelers Release Aaron Rodgers Following Criticism of Coach
stories.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have released quarterback Aaron Rodgers shortly after he publicly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on 'The Pat McAfee Show.' Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and missing walkthroughs, leading to tensions within the team. Steelers president Art Rooney II stated that 'insubordination will not be tolerated' in light of the incident.

stories.title: Mass Protests Erupt in Iraqi Kurdistan Against Baghdad's Oil Control Plans
